citation.title: DQN-Based Pre-Optimization for Dual-Scale Collaborative Topology Optimization of Anisotropic Materials
citation.authors: Shuo Feng, Yuhao Yang, Ke Li, Qidong Han, Jinchen Cao, Junyi Du
citation.venue: Applied Sciences 16(9), 4080 (MDPI; published 22 April 2026; open access, CC BY)
citation.version_coded: Version of record, publisher PDF (26 pp.) from MDPI's file server (mdpi-res.com, the target of the article's PDF link), read in full as text; the www.mdpi.com pages returned HTTP 403 to the generic User-Agent

included.reason: I-QUALITY (screened I-SPEED; the abstract's only quantitative classical comparison is compliance)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: On the MBB beam, running the dual-scale thermo-mechanical optimization from a DQN pre-optimized start gave final compliance 0.5754 versus 0.7421 for the same framework without DQN pre-optimization, 22.463% lower.
claim.key_phrase: achieves a 22.463% reduction in structural compliance
claim.location: Abstract (quantitative comparison with the traditional method); values in Sec. 5.1 (p. 17) and the Introduction (p. 2)
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No runtime is reported for any method, and the baseline's iteration count is not stated. The abstract's faster-convergence claim is qualitative; Table 3 (p. 12) lists 60-180 iterations for the eight DQN runs only. Not derivable.
claim.alternatives: (1) Abstract and Sec. 3.3, qualitative: dynamic penalty tuning accelerates convergence and cuts BESO iterations; no times or baseline iteration counts anywhere (speed stratum if chosen, with R1 fail for lack of any number). (2) Abstract: better thermal management than traditional methods, not quantified against a classical run. (3) Sec. 5.2 (pp. 17-18): anisotropic vs isotropic microstructures within the proposed framework, 0.3272 vs 0.5754 (43.14% lower); not a classical comparison. (4) Table 3: eight DQN seeds on the MBB beam, normalized final compliance 105.51-109.14 (mean 108.23, SD 1.14); no baseline in the table.

baseline.classical_method: The same dual-scale thermo-mechanical optimization without DQN pre-optimization: SIMP-type interpolation of modulus, conductivity and thermal-stress coefficient with a fixed empirical penalty factor (value not stated), OC update with move limit, uniform initial density 0.5 (Sec. 2.4, 4, 5.1, pp. 5-17). The article calls the optimizer BESO, but the stated update is the OC rule (Eq. 23)
baseline.implementation: not stated; the TO runs in a numerical-analysis environment and the DQN in PyTorch 2.6.0, CPU version (Sec. 3.3-3.4, pp. 7-8)
baseline.hardware_ml: CPU (PyTorch 2.6.0 CPU version, Sec. 3.4, p. 8); processor not stated
baseline.problem_size: Macro 150 × 80 elements, volume fraction 0.4; micro unit cell 50 × 50 elements, volume fraction 0.5 (Table 4, p. 16). Sec. 5.4 also uses 300 × 100 (MBB) and 150 × 100 (cantilever) without a baseline
baseline.classical_iterations: not stated for the baseline; convergence tolerance 0.01 on the design change (Table 4, p. 16); the DQN runs needed 60-180 iterations (Table 3, p. 12)
baseline.training_time: not stated; the DQN is trained online during the optimization and updated after each iteration (Sec. 3.4, p. 8)
baseline.data_generation_cost: none; no offline dataset (online per-problem training, Sec. 3.4)
baseline.quality_metric: Final mechanical compliance (c value) of the optimized design from the optimizer's FE analysis [inferred]; normalized compliance histories (Fig. 8); thermal compliance and average temperature in the weighting study (Sec. 5.3, Table 5)
baseline.quality_gap: MBB: 0.5754 with DQN pre-optimization vs 0.7421 without, 22.463% lower (Sec. 5.1, p. 17). The baseline design keeps many intermediate densities, grey values 0.2-0.8 (Fig. 7a, p. 16). Achieved volume fractions are not reported for either design

R1.evidence: Sec. 5.1 (pp. 16-17), Table 4, Figs. 7-8: both designs share the mesh, loads and nominal volume fraction 0.4. Matching is loose: the baseline's penalty value, filter, iteration count and stopping rule are not stated; it ends with many intermediate densities (Fig. 7a), so a penalized grey field is compared with a near-binary design [inferred]; achieved volumes are not reported; which of the eight DQN runs (Table 3) gives 0.5754 is not stated; no compute budget is compared.

R2.evidence: Quality stratum, competence of the comparator. Sec. 5.1: the baseline is the authors' own run without DQN, with an unstated fixed ('empirical') penalty and a uniform 0.5 start. Its grey final layout (Fig. 7a) suggests an under-penalized or unconverged run [inferred], while the DQN runs end with penalties 2.4-5.0 (Table 3). No classical run with a standard penalty or continuation schedule is tried, so the 22.463% gain may reflect the penalty choice rather than the DQN [judgment]. Markers (a)-(e) do not bear on a quality claim; unsure between pass and partial.

R3.evidence: Quality stratum with per-problem online DQN training and no offline dataset (Sec. 3.4); no speed claim is quantified. For C3: no DQN training time, pre-optimization time or TO time is reported.

R4.evidence: Sec. 5.1-5.5: the compliance values are the optimizer's FE results for the returned designs [inferred]. Achieved volume fractions are not reported for any design, and failed or non-converged runs are not counted. Eight seeds are reported for the DQN method (Table 3), while the baseline is a single run. The 3D extrusions (Fig. 12) are not analysed (Sec. 5.6).

reporting.n_test_cases: Classical comparison: 1 case (MBB beam, 150 × 80 macro mesh, Sec. 5.1). Other studies without a baseline: 3 microstructure groups (Sec. 5.2), 4 MBB and 3 cantilever weightings (Sec. 5.3, 5.5), MBB 300 × 100 and cantilever 150 × 100 (Sec. 5.4), 8 DQN seeds (Table 3)

notes: Screening code was I-SPEED; full text gives stratum Q because the abstract's only quantitative comparison with the traditional method is the 22.463% compliance reduction, and no runtime or baseline iteration count appears anywhere. The comparator is a classical (non-learned) run of the same optimization, so this is not FT-NOBASELINE. The DQN is trained online inside each optimization (Sec. 3.4), so R3 is n/a. dim coded 2d: all optimization is 2D; the 3D result is a linear extrusion with no analysis (Sec. 5.6). seeds_or_variance = yes for the DQN method only (8 seeds, mean 108.23, SD 1.14; Table 3). Internal inconsistencies: the title and abstract name BESO, but the method sections describe SIMP interpolation with an OC update (Eqs. 8-10, 23); Table 3 gives normalized final compliances of about 105-109, while Sec. 5.1 gives 0.5754 for the pre-optimized MBB design, with no explanation of the two normalizations; in Table 5 (rendered page 21) the 0.8-weight row repeats the thermal compliance (4.1504) and average temperature (677.96) of the 0.6-weight row, while the Sec. 5.3 text gives 4.1874 for that weight. Table 3 (rendered page 12) lists 60-180 iterations per DQN run; four of the eight runs stop at 180. Data availability: contributions are included in the article, further inquiries to the corresponding author; no code statement. Hardware: only the DQN device class (CPU) is stated. retest_candidate false: no code and no speed claim. No author named Jun Wang.
